operators.description: Load nation table (25 rows) into a direct array nationkey→name. Identify nationkeys for FRANCE and GERMANY.

For each row from shared lineitem scan (shipdate 1995-1996, ~18.8M rows): (1) probe hash_supplier_by_suppkey on l_suppkey to get s_nationkey, (2) early-filter: s_nationkey IN {france_key, germany_key} — eliminates ~92% of rows, (3) probe hash_orders_by_orderkey on l_orderkey to get o_custkey, (4) probe hash_customer_by_custkey on o_custkey to get c_nationkey, (5) filter: c_nationkey IN {france_key, germany_key}, (6) cross-filter: (s_nationkey=france_key AND c_nationkey=germany_key) OR (s_nationkey=germany_key AND c_nationkey=france_key)

probes.note: Probe supplier first — smallest hash (100K entries, ~5.5MB, L3-resident). Early nation filter on supplier side eliminates ~92% immediately before expensive orders/customer probes.

operators.cross_filter: (s_nationkey == france_key AND c_nationkey == germany_key) OR (s_nationkey == germany_key AND c_nationkey == france_key)

operators.description: Compute derived columns for surviving rows

Group by (supp_nation, cust_nation, l_year). Only 2 nation values × 2 nation values × 2 years = max 4 valid groups after cross-filter. Use a small fixed array indexed by (nation_pair_id, year_offset). No hash table needed.
operators.note: With only 4 possible groups, use a flat array of 4 accumulators. Zero hash overhead, perfect cache behavior. Thread-local arrays merged at end.

operators.description: Materialize the 4 result rows from the direct array, sort by (supp_nation, cust_nation, l_year) ASC.
operators.note: With ≤4 rows, sorting is trivial — insertion sort or hardcoded comparison.

parallelism.partitioning: Morsel-driven over scan_lineitem_shipdate_1995_1996 output. Each thread has a local array[4] of SUM accumulators. Final merge: single-threaded sum of 4-element arrays from all threads — negligible cost.

thread_local_state.description: One SUM accumulator per (nation_pair, year) combination

execution_notes.probe_order_rationale: Probe supplier hash first (5.5MB, L3-resident) and apply nation filter immediately. This eliminates ~92% of rows before probing the larger orders hash (750MB) and customer hash (300MB), dramatically reducing cache pressure on those larger structures.
execution_notes.fused_pipeline: Steps 1-3 are fused into a single tight loop per morsel: probe → filter → compute → accumulate. No intermediate materialization.
